summary.title: Good sleep, good learning, good life
summary.one_liner: Sleep is essential for memory consolidation and learning, and this e-book by Piotr Wozniak explains the biology of sleep and practical steps for better sleep.
keywords: why do we need to sleep
takeaways: Sleep is required for consolidating learned material into long-term memory, so cutting sleep (e.g. cramming before exams) reduces recall.
The hippocampus stores short-term memory patterns, and sleep is when these are encoded into the neocortex, per Buzsaki's two-stage model as summarized by the author.
Sleep deprivation has serious health and safety costs, including fatigue-related accidents and effects on immune function and brain health.

Practical advice includes avoiding alarm clocks where possible, trying free running sleep for insomnia and sleep phase problems, and avoiding sleep-regulating substances such as sleeping pills, alcohol, nicotine and caffeine.
summary.summary: This long essay-style e-book by Dr Piotr Wozniak, written for the SuperMemo site and revised over 2000 to 2018, synthesizes sleep research with a focus on learning, creativity, and practical sleep improvement. It covers the claimed role of sleep in memory consolidation, the hippocampus and neocortex, sleep deprivation risks, and social habits that undermine sleep. It also offers practical guidance such as free running sleep and a highlights list. The author notes that the science is changing quickly, cites research with contradictory views, and urges readers to consult other sources.
